clue.text: See 24
Straight there, after travelling round

indicators.note: travelling suggests moving about, so the letters of the word there are set in a new order

parts.note: a round shape is a ring, the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone is told to go straight there, after making a detour round the houses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'travelling' rearranges the letters to HETER; 'Straight' is slang here, not a direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Straight is slang for heterosexual, and hetero is the clipped form of that word.

clue.text: Unadventurous guy? Then the woman stripped off

parts.note: a guy is a rope holding a tent or mast steady, which is also called a stay

indicators.note: off can mean bad or wrong, so the letters gathered here are mixed up
stripped means the word woman loses its outer covering, its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A dull man is described, and then a woman takes her clothes off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stripped' peels the outer letters off to leave OMA; 'off' mixes that with the article to make ATHOME. A guy is a tent rope, not a man.
explanation.definitionFit: A stay-at-home person prefers their own house to travel or excitement, so the word describes an unadventurous character.

clue.text: Small-minded? Afraid so!

parts.note: S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
to have minded something is to have cared about it

explanation.surface: Someone accused of being petty answers that, yes, they really are frightened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small-minded' looks like one word but splits into S and CARED.
explanation.definitionFit: Scared and afraid are plain synonyms for being frightened.

clue.text: Conservatives behind the Times newspaper, not the Scotsman

parts.note: something behind the times is out of date, or old

indicators.note: not tells the solver to leave out the Scotsman from the newspaper's name

parts.note: the Guardian is the newspaper that publishes this very crossword
Ian is a typically Scottish man's name, so a crossword Scotsman

explanation.surface: Traditionalists who lag behind the Times newspaper but not the Scotsman, two rival British papers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' and 'Scotsman' look like newspapers alongside 'newspaper', but only the Guardian is meant; 'not' removes IAN from GUARDIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The old guard is the long-standing group in any body who resist change, its conservatives.

clue.text: Stood next to current queen

parts.note: to stand for office is to run for it, so stood gives ran
I is the symbol for electric current in physics

explanation.surface: A person stood beside the reigning monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stood' here means stood as a candidate.
explanation.definitionFit: A rani is a Hindu queen or the wife of a raja.

clue.text: Well-off area: right district selected originally for a Keith or Gordon?

definitions.note: Keith Richards and Gordon Richards both bear the surname, so either is 'a Richards'

parts.note: well-off means wealthy, or rich

indicators.note: originally points to the start of each of the following words, taking just the opening letters

explanation.surface: A wealthy neighbourhood is described in estate-agent shorthand, ending with a question about men's names.
explanation.walkthrough: Keith Richards is the Rolling Stones guitarist; Sir Gordon Richards was a champion British jockey.
explanation.definitionFit: Each famous man shares this surname, so the question mark marks a definition by example.

clue.text: Doctor X, vegan animal rights activist

parts.note: MO, medical officer, is a common crossword doctor
the multiplication sign is read as 'by', as in three by four

explanation.surface: A medical practitioner, Dr X, campaigns for animals and eats no animal products.
explanation.walkthrough: Moby is the American musician, a well-known vegan campaigner. 'Doctor X' looks like an anonymous name, but X is the multiplication sign, read as 'by'.
explanation.definitionFit: The musician Moby is famous for his outspoken veganism and animal welfare campaigning, so the description identifies him.

clue.text: Papers can't lie? Wrong, just the same

parts.note: identity papers are ID

indicators.note: wrong suggests something put incorrectly, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone insists documents don't lie, only to be told they are mistaken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrong' rearranges CANTLIE into ENTICAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Identical means exactly alike, which is what just the same says.

clue.text: Is Puck good? Ring a friend

parts.note: Puck is the setter, so 'is Puck?' becomes 'am I?' in his own voice
a ring is round, like the letter O

explanation.surface: The setter wonders if he is any good, and decides to phone a pal.
explanation.walkthrough: Puck is the setter's pseudonym, so his question about himself is AM I.
explanation.definitionFit: Amigo is Spanish for friend, widely used in English for a pal.

clue.text: Some 'iffy' remedies returned? On the surface, that's rough

indicators.note: returned means the letters are read in the opposite direction
some signals that only part of the following words is used, the letters run across them

explanation.surface: Dubious remedies are sent back because they feel coarse when applied.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' picks YREME from 'iffY REMEdies'; 'returned' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Emery is a gritty abrasive coated on boards and paper, giving them a rough surface for filing and smoothing.

clue.text: Upset our shy girl right away, as a rascal might

indicators.note: to upset something is to overturn it, so the letters are put in a new order
away tells the solver to send off the letter for right from the words

explanation.surface: Someone upsets a bashful girl, behaving like a scamp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right away' removes one R from OURSHYGIRL; 'Upset' rearranges what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Roguishly means mischievously or impishly, the manner of a rogue or rascal.

clue.text: Saw son cut down to 1, for easier assimilation

parts.note: S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

parts.words: cut down to 1, for easier assimilation
parts.note: 1 is the answer at 1-down, SIZE; potted means cut down to size, abridged so it is easier to take in

explanation.surface: A son was trimmed to a smaller form so he would fit in more easily.
explanation.walkthrough: The 1 sends the solver to 1-down, SIZE: 'cut down to size, for easier assimilation' describes a potted history.
explanation.definitionFit: To have spotted something is to have caught sight of it, the past tense of see.

clue.text: Humming after crossword essentially well-constructed

indicators.note: after places the smelly word behind the central letter
essentially points to the essence, the very centre, of the word that follows

parts.note: humming is slang for smelling bad; olid is a rare word meaning foul-smelling

explanation.surface: Someone hums after a crossword that was basically well made.
explanation.walkthrough: 'essentially' takes the central S of CROSSWORD; 'Humming' means stinking, which is OLID.
explanation.definitionFit: Something solid is sturdy and well built, so it fits well-constructed.

clue.text: Another married lover

indicators.note: another form of the word married gives a different arrangement of its letters

explanation.surface: A married person has a further lover on the side.
explanation.definitionFit: An admirer is a suitor or romantic follower, so a lover in the broad sense.

clue.text: Flute? Part played is routine

definitions.meaning: Flute is one of the 'rude ...', the workmen who stage a play in A Midsummer Night's Dream

explanation.surface: A flute part in a performance comes across as dull and automatic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flute' looks like the instrument, but it is Francis Flute, the bellows-mender in Shakespeare's comedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's tradesmen are called mechanicals, and a mechanical task is one done without thought.

clue.text: After tip-off, gets hold of fruit

indicators.note: tip-off means the very tip, the first letter, is taken off the word

parts.note: someone who gets hold of something grasps it

explanation.surface: After receiving a tip-off, someone seizes some fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tip-off' looks like a warning but tells you to drop the first letter of GRASPS.
explanation.definitionFit: Rasps is an old or dialect word for raspberries, a soft red fruit.

clue.text: Game is second sale item not won

parts.note: an item at an auction sale is a lot

indicators.note: not tells the solver to leave the letter for won out of the number

parts.note: second in a list is number two
W stands for won in sports tables

explanation.surface: A game turns out to be the second item in a sale that nobody won.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not won' takes W out of TWO, leaving TO.
explanation.definitionFit: Lotto is a game of chance played by drawing numbers, a lottery.

clue.text: Farm vehicle turned up, worked into drawing

indicators.note: in a down entry, turned up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a cart is a farm vehicle

indicators.note: worked suggests something being kneaded or reshaped, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A farm vehicle arrived and was worked into a sketch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reverses CART to TRAC; 'worked' rearranges INTO to TION.
explanation.definitionFit: Traction is the act of drawing or pulling a load, as a traction engine does.

clue.text: Department investigating contracted detective's retirement

indicators.note: retirement suggests withdrawing backwards, so the letters are read in the opposite order
contracted means shortened, losing the last letter

parts.note: dick is old slang for a detective

explanation.surface: A department looks into a shortened detective's retirement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contracted' cuts DICK to DIC; 'retirement' turns it round. The CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of British police.
explanation.definitionFit: The CID is the police department that investigates crime, its name ending in Investigation Department.

clue.text: Unfaithful lover is 4 after straying

indicators.note: letters that have strayed have wandered out of place, so these are rearranged

parts.note: 4 refers to the answer at 4-down, SCARED

explanation.surface: A cheating partner is frightened after having wandered off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after straying' rearranges the letters. Cressida is the Trojan woman who deserts Troilus for Diomedes.
explanation.definitionFit: Cressida betrays Troilus in the medieval and Shakespearean story, so she is the classic faithless lover.

clue.text: Lots of actors originally starred in a musical

indicators.note: in places the first letter inside the show's name

parts.note: Cats is the Andrew Lloyd Webber musical

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Plenty of performers originally starred in a stage musical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' takes S from 'starred'; 'in' puts it inside CATS.
explanation.definitionFit: A cast is the company of actors in a show, so lots of actors are casts.

clue.text: Crack marksman departed with detective

parts.note: the departed are the dead
a private eye is a detective

explanation.surface: An expert shot has died, and a detective is on the case.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadeye is an expert shot who rarely misses, a nickname as in Deadeye Dick.

clue.text: Name saint or pope? Brother no longer can

definitions.note: Francis is a first name, the saint of Assisi, and the current pope's chosen name

indicators.note: no longer means the following word is taken off the end

parts.note: a Franciscan is a friar, a religious brother

explanation.surface: Someone asks for a saint or pope to be named; a monk says he cannot any more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brother no longer can' drops CAN from FRANCISCAN, a friar of St Francis's order.
explanation.definitionFit: Francis is a common Christian name, borne by St Francis of Assisi and by Pope Francis.

clue.text: Death of European with no middle name

indicators.note: with no middle tells the solver to drop the central letter of the word

parts.note: a Finnish person is a European

explanation.surface: A European dies who had no middle name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no middle name' removes the central N of FINNISH.
explanation.definitionFit: Finish can mean end or downfall, as in the expression 'a fight to the finish'.

clue.text: Lots of people, 8 being the 25th of them?

definitions.meaning: 8 is MOBY: mobs, numbered from MOB A, then MOB Y is the twenty-fifth

explanation.surface: Masses of people, with someone counting one of them as twenty-fifth.
explanation.walkthrough: Lettering mobs alphabetically, Y is the 25th letter, so MOBY at 8-down is the 25th mob.
explanation.definitionFit: A crowd is a large gathering, also called a mob, which the second reading relies on.

clue.text: Artist back in stock, in refined Colorado town

indicators.note: the first in places the painter inside the rearranged letters
refined means processed or reworked, so the letters are rearranged
back means the abbreviation is written in reverse

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, is a standard crossword artist

explanation.surface: A painter is back in stock in some sophisticated town in Colorado.
explanation.walkthrough: 'refined' rearranges STOCK and IN to KITCSON; 'back' turns RA to AR, put 'in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Kit Carson is a small town in Colorado named after the frontiersman.

clue.text: Long for the longer sleepers perhaps half of LNER and one third of LMS used

definitions.text: Long for the longer sleepers perhaps

parts.note: the second half of LNER is ER, Edwardus Rex, the royal cipher standing for a monarch on the throne
the last third of LMS is S, the label on the smallest garment grade, standing for how big a thing is (large, medium, small)

explanation.surface: Railway history: sleeper trains of the old LNER and LMS companies, Britain's prewar railways.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces work backwards: ER, half of LNER, abbreviates KING, and S, a third of LMS, abbreviates SIZE. LNER and LMS were two of Britain's 'Big Four' railway companies before 1948.
explanation.definitionFit: King-size describes something extra long, like cigarettes, and beds made longer for tall sleepers.

clue.text: Attention-seeking expression in article by the Edge

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
a hem is the edge of a piece of cloth

explanation.surface: A newspaper article sits beside a guitarist known as the Edge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Edge' suggests U2's guitarist, but it is simply a hem.
explanation.definitionFit: Ahem is the throat-clearing noise someone makes to draw attention.

clue.text: Creamy-white, like a Welshman?

parts.note: Ivor is a typically Welsh man's name
the suffix -y makes an adjective meaning like, as in silky

explanation.surface: Something pale cream in colour is compared to a man from Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: IVOR-Y reads as 'Ivor-like', a playful adjective from the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivory is the creamy white colour of elephant tusks.

clue.text: More than one solver yet to finish? Child's play, perhaps, using this

indicators.note: more than one copy here means the word is written twice
yet to finish means the word stops short of its last letter

parts.note: the solver is addressed as you

explanation.surface: A crossword solver hasn't finished, and the puzzle turns out to be child's play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yet to finish' cuts YOU to YO; 'More than one' doubles it.
explanation.definitionFit: A yo-yo is a spinning toy on a string, something children play with.

clue.text: Stoned female content to down 10 beers

indicators.note: content means only what is held inside, so the outer letters at each end of the phrase are stripped away

parts.note: the words are taken as written, except the number 10, read as the letters I and O that its digits resemble

explanation.surface: A drunk woman is willing to knock back ten beers.
explanation.walkthrough: In effect a hidden word: read 10 as IO and the answer sits inside 'dowN IO BEers'. 'content to' keeps only the inside, dropping DOW and ERS.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Niobe was turned to stone after her children were killed, so she is the petrified woman.

clue.text: Playing darts, lady is mean and wicked!

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are being moved about in play, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman throwing darts is nasty and cruel.
explanation.definitionFit: Dastardly means despicably cruel or underhand, a villainous quality.
